title: Why do we have fingerprints?
examples: Why are fingerprints so important for police officers?
Can I lose my fingerprints someday?

explain.say: Say you know that fingerprints are special lines on your fingers.
Say fingerprints help people know who you really are.
Say every single person has fingerprints that look different.
Say your fingerprints help you hold things or write your name.

draw.text: Prints help with grip and writing.

explain.say: Say when you touch something, the oils on your fingers leave a print.

draw.text: Oils leave a print on surfaces.

explain.say: Say even if you and a friend touch the same thing, your prints are different.

faq.q: Do all people have the same fingerprints?
faq.a: No, every person has a unique set of fingerprints. This means no two people share the exact same print.
Scientists think fingerprints help us grip things better and help identify us. They are part of how our skin develops.
asks: What is the job of fingerprints?
Why are these lines on my fingers?

faq.q: Can fingerprints change when I get older?
faq.a: Generally, your basic fingerprint patterns do not change throughout your life. They stay the same from when you are a baby.

faq.q: Are fingerprints only used by police?
faq.a: No, they are used in many places for identification, like airports or even unlocking phones. It is a very useful tool.
asks: Are fingerprints just for crime solving?

faq.q: Are fingerprints the same on all fingers?
faq.a: No, the pattern can be different on each finger. Sometimes the patterns on your thumb are different from your index finger.
asks: Do all fingers have the same print?
Is the print the same everywhere?

facts: Fingerprints are patterns of ridges on the skin.
These patterns are unique to every individual person.
They help us grip objects and are used for identification.
The patterns are formed while we are growing in the womb.

options.show: They help identify who a person is.
options.say: They help identify who a person is.

wrong.1: While they help grip, their main use is identification.
